newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DOLLAR/MARK LIFTED BY SHORT-COVERING IN SINGAPORE.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR/MARK LIFTED BY SHORT-COVERING IN SINGAPORE.

text.p: The U.S. dollar was lifted by some short-covering against the mark at midday on Thursday, but Singapore dealers said it could come under renewed pressure.
"Far East players got a bit worried and sold down the dollar/mark after its overnight move. But now there's some short-covering interest from the 1.8220/30 mark level," a U.S. bank dealer said.

Dealers said the mark was being bought back against most crosses, especially the yen and sterling, after the Bundesbank said in its monthly report on Wednesday that the pace of inflation had picked up, sparking fears of a German rate hike.
"On dollar/mark, there's still a possibility of flushing out some stale longs. Some people have a short-term target of 1.8220/50," the dealer said.
"But we should see some new money coming in at those levels," he added.
Dealers said the dollar was consolidating within a broader 114-117 yen range, but should eventually head higher as the Japanese economy remained in the doldrums.
"The Japanese have too many problems to consider raising rates because that would only give the economy another blow," the trader said.
